name: Groundwater Flow and Pollution Modelling
description: Modelling concepts and constructing various kinds of models for addressing soil water and groundwater quantity and quality problems of real-world settings; subsurface processes in soil, rocks and aquifers; unsaturated zone properties: soil moisture levels, retention curves, and hydraulic parameters; unsaturated and saturated flows through porous media; infiltration and wetting front; agricultural water and groundwater recharge; single and multiple aquifer systems; fracture flows; multiphase flows; groundwater contamination, sources and causes of groundwater pollution; anthropogenic and geogenic pollution; contaminant transport mechanisms: advection, dispersion, diffusion, adsorption, biodegradation, radioactive decay, reactive processes, and geochemical processes; hydrodynamics dispersion, plume evolution and pollution dynamics; multiphase contamination: NAPLs, VOCs; numerical models: finite difference and finite element methods, numerical modelling of steady and transient flows in saturated and unsaturated domains, contaminant transport modelling; regional aquifer simulation; contaminated groundwater systems and their rehabilitation; integrated use of numerical modelling, optimization and geospatial techniques, geostatistics, and fuzzy theory for groundwater vulnerability assessment, environmental impact assessment and groundwater management; applications and case studies; site specific groundwater quality problems in Indian context.
